Pain_Category: Which pain category/combination triggers this rule
Pain_Severity_Threshold: Minimum pain score/severity required to trigger rule
Required_Readiness: Readiness dimension(s) and minimum score required
Recommended_VH_Domain: Care Delivery / Digital Twin / Workforce Simulation / Immersive Training
Reasoning: Short explanation of why this rule maps to this recommendation
Evidence_Level: Strength of evidence backing this rule: Low / Medium / High
Priority: Priority/order in which this rule should be evaluated, 1 = highest

Pain_Category: Bed capacity shortage + high digital readiness
Reasoning: High bed pressure combined with strong digital infrastructure supports hospital-at-home / virtual ward models

Pain_Category: Bed capacity shortage + geographic/specialist access barriers
Reasoning: Health systems with severe bed/access pressure and strong EHR-integrated telehealth infrastructure have successfully deployed hospital-at-home and virtual care hub models (e.g., Mercy Virtual, Kaiser Permanente, Mass General Brigham, Atrium Health, Mayo Clinic)

Organizations with strong financial readiness and an existing ROI model have used hospital-at-home to reduce readmission penalties and avoid costly inpatient stays (e.g., Atrium Health's sub-1.0 readmission O/E ratio)

Pain_Category: Inefficient scheduling/utilization (e.g., high clinic no-show rates)
Reasoning: Discrete-event simulation digital twins have reduced scheduling inefficiencies even without advanced AI capability, as at Indiana University Health Arnett Hospital

Pain_Category: Bed/ward capacity constraints needing operational modeling
Reasoning: Ward-level digital twins let hospitals test staffing and bed-allocation policies before real-world implementation, as demonstrated in NHS hospital digital-twin pilots
Academic medical centers have begun building digital twins specifically to predict staff burnout trajectories and inform workforce planning, as at Virginia Tech Carilion School of Medicine

Pain_Category: Patient safety / procedural skill gaps requiring risk-free practice
Pain_Severity_Threshold: Not pain-severity-based; driven by training-gap identification
Reasoning: VR and manikin-based simulation centers (Johns Hopkins Medicine Simulation Center) and cloud-based sandbox platforms (SIIM Virtual Hospital Platform) let organizations train staff on high-stakes procedures and enterprise imaging workflows without patient risk
